proposals.name: Provider-clock ceiling on each tool round: the interval between two server-minted request ids bounds every client-side duration claim for the call between them
proposals.observation_summary: Anthropic request ids decode as UUIDv7 (unix ms) in 154,815/154,815 swechat requests, against 2,418.98 expected by chance, and in 31,085/31,085 cc_local requests. The layout is inferred from data and is UNVERIFIED against documentation. The swechat n includes 50 Vertex ids that the loader stored as message ids (ids O1). The decoded server time agrees with client stamps in 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] when every copy is counted; the full-data p50 offset is 3,781 ms [3,684, 3,871] (ids O2). One constant skew per stream brackets every id in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat streams, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], interval width p50 2,268 ms. A placebo that moves one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441 streams, but moving it later flags 10, the baseline. The bracket therefore catches back-dating only, at per-turn resolution (ids O5, skeptic). aiv_cu Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini server ids show 0 violations against row inserts; OpenAI and Gemini ids have 1 s resolution (ids O3). The clocks that fail are client clocks: cc_local has 125 violations in 3 sessions, down to -7,749 ms (ids O6). Positive control: in the 2 re-stamped resume/fork session pairs, the request-id clock separates the copies (disagreeing offsets at least 619,473 ms vs agreeing 2,347-21,734 ms). The skeptic notes the re-stamp is also visible without the id clock, and n is 2 pairs (ids O7). In aiv_cu, Gemini's server-timing duration fits inside the logger's row gap with 0/12292 violations (min slack 563.8 ms), and rows never precede the HTTP Date (min 78.2 ms) (two_clocks O7). The Date header has 1 s resolution (D19). Harness timers already sit inside the client window: Glob 1/2090, Task 0/1023, Agent 0/1886 (two_clocks O8), and the bash_progress floor rule holds in 0/112677 events (two_clocks O9). Not yet measured: any client timer against the server interval between two request ids.
proposals.test_measurement: Data: raw swechat Claude Code transcripts (fix tolerances on split A, test on B) and cc_local; aiv_cu Gemini rows for the header variant. (1) Decode t_req for every assistant entry's requestId with the O1 decoder, and drop duplicate copies of shared ids (O7). (2) For each main-thread stream (session x agent), order requests by t_req. For each tool_use in response k whose tool_result is sent with request k+1, compute S = t_req(k+1) - t_req(k). Both ends are server times, so client skew cancels. Exclude run_in_background, Workflow and async Agent launches. (3) Compare S with every client-side duration claim for that round: the call->result timestamp gap; bash_progress max elapsedTimeSeconds; Glob/WebFetch/WebSearch durationMs; Task/Agent totalDurationMs; mcp_progress elapsedTimeMs. Flag D > S + tol, with tol fixed on split A before looking at B. Report the violation rate per timer type with session-clustered CIs, and the honest slack distribution (S - D)/S, which sets the smallest detectable overclaim factor. (4) Power: on B, inflate one call's durations by x2/x5/x10 and by +5/+30/+300 s (the O5 placebo design) and report flag rates. (5) Gemini variant in aiv_cu: S_g = (HTTP Date(k+1) - server-timing dur(k+1)) - HTTP Date(k), at 1 s resolution. This is the only per-round timing aiv_cu has, so test it against durations printed in shell results.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: re-stamped resume/fork copies, which give 190 offsets above 10 min when every copy is counted (ids O2) in 2 session pairs (ids O7); dedupe them before testing. Background or async launches whose result returns before the work ends: in cc_local the parent result precedes the last nested event in 63/63 Workflow/Agent calls, and 7/7 Agent calls had run_in_background=true (two_clocks O15); exclude these. 1 s resolution of OpenAI/Gemini ids and of the HTTP Date (ids O3, D19); tolerance must exceed it. Absorbed rather than false-alarming: client clock skew (ids O6) and machine suspend. In the one timer-over-timeout case, elapsed was 901 s against a 300000 ms timeout (two_clocks O10). Both interval ends are server times, and a suspended client sends its next request late. Unmeasured: clock skew between the provider servers minting consecutive ids; retry attempts; concurrent subagent streams (use only the parent stream's consecutive requests).
proposals.evasion_cost: Live fabrication (a lying tool backend, with the forger also writing the log): to make a round claim D seconds of work, the forger must hold the next API request for at least D, because the provider stamps receipt. Time can be padded but not compressed, so the cost is real wall-clock per fabricated call. Post-hoc retiming or inserting a round requires the forger to re-mint every affected request id: base58 UUIDv7 behind 'req_01', version 7, variant 2, chosen ms, plausible random bits. Each id must sit inside its stream's skew bracket and keep its order. Message ids must follow the format epoch (UUIDv7 only after 2026-07-06, ids O4). This is cheap for anyone who knows the layout; the ids note says these ids are unsigned. Re-minting becomes infeasible only if the verifier can look request ids up in the provider's own records, which was not tested here (UNVERIFIED). The model never sees request ids, Date or server-timing headers in its context and cannot predict server receipt times.
proposals.coverage: Measured: every Anthropic request in swechat CC (154,815 ids, 3,674 streams) and cc_local (31,085 ids). aiv_cu Gemini rows with timing headers: 12292 rows in 347 of 2000 B sessions (two_clocks O7). aiv_cc has 0 request ids stored (ids O13), so coverage there is 0. In aiv_cu, call and result share one stamp (lat == 0 for 59,956/59,956 calls, correlations O4), so the server interval would be the only per-round timing. The share of tool calls whose issuing and carrying requests both have ids in one stream is unmeasured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Reading timestamps out of UUIDv7 is standard. My guess is that using the interval between two provider-minted request ids as a skew-free ceiling on client-claimed tool durations is uncommon. It adds nothing at capture time, unlike Hearsay, ACE or Tracekit. Prior art on forensic use of server-side request timestamps needs checking.
proposals.rank_reason: This is the only observed clock minted outside the forger's control, and it is present on every Anthropic request. Live fakery must pay real time, but post-hoc fakery stays cheap until provider lookup exists.

proposals.name: Commit-time freeze points: the git-held usage tally and agent_changes, amplified by the prompt-cache chain
proposals.observation_summary: At commit time the Entire CLI writes a 5-integer usage tally per session into checkpoint metadata in git. The tally equals an exact (tolerance 0) recount of the stored transcript in 4794/4836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions: full 2772, prefix 1664, window 358, none 42. In the prefix class the snapshot was taken while the session continued: created_at precedes the last transcript timestamp in 1664/1664 prefix sessions vs 39/2772 full ones, with a median of 3 messages past the snapshot (T1). The declared offset explains window sessions 357/357 (T2). After the dataset join fix, 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] remain unmatched (T3). Skeptic correction (T1): the tally recounts the transcript's own usage fields, so its only independent content is that it is a commit-time snapshot. agent_changes in the same commits copies Edit/Write inputs; 84335/95892 = 0.879 [0.863, 0.895] entries match a call on the exact key (commit_witness O7). Checkpoints are replicated: 1825 of 11581 checkpoint_ids appear in more than one repo (T9), and 4023 agent_changes entries trace to a same-name repo under another owner (commit_witness O7). Usage cascades along the cache chain, cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k). The chain holds exactly in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1), and in 59747/59804 aiv_cc pairs, run-clustered 0.99905 (aiv_accounting O9). Edits that leave usage untouched are caught only when large. At FPR 1%, the insertion detectable at power 0.5/0.9 is 8913/10000 chars (D_abs) and 6310/7079 chars (D_asym) in swechat CC, and 2239/2512 (D_abs) and 1778/2512 (D_asym) in aiv_cc (TC2). Edits to results under 1k chars are never detected (TC16).
proposals.test_measurement: Data: swechat Claude-format sessions with a matched tally (T1 full, prefix and window classes), their raw transcripts, checkpoint_metadata_raw and commits.agent_changes. (a) Freeze coverage: per session, the share of tool results timestamped before the snapshot boundary (whole transcript, prefix end, or the declared window), with session-clustered CIs. (b) Cascade amplification: for each frozen result j, count m_j, the later responses in the same unbroken cache chain inside the frozen span. A usage-consistent edit of delta tokens shifts the tally's cache_read sum by delta*m_j and cache_creation by delta. Simulate delta = 1 and delta = the TC2 threshold on every frozen result, re-run the T1 matcher, and report the share that flips from matched to none. (c) The forger's other option, editing text but not usage: report the TC2 power curve restricted to frozen spans. (d) Change one character of a frozen Edit/Write input, re-run the commit_witness O7 exact-key trace, and report the flip rate. (e) Replicas: per checkpoint, the number of repos that hold it (T9). These are copies a forger would also have to rewrite.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest floor: 33/5701 sessions unmatched after the join fix (T3). The rate is highest in CLI 0.5.x, 15/1048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235] (T4). With output_tokens excluded, the Claude residuals classify as prefix 7, full 1, none 6, consistent with mid-stream snapshots (T4). In the dataset table, multi-checkpoint rows mix snapshots (39 sessions, T3); use the session_logs values. 1010 agent_changes entries appear in no released transcript, and 6524 belong to another session of the same repo (commit_witness O7), so the trace needs the checkpoint's wider session window. Cache-chain breaks from images, compaction and idle gaps stop the amplification at the break (aiv_accounting O9).
proposals.evasion_cost: Live fabrication evades this completely. The model really consumed the fake output, the provider counted it, and Entire snapshots the forged log. Post-hoc editing of a frozen span leaves two options. (a) Leave usage untouched. The edit must then stay below the conservation threshold: 6310 (D_asym) to 8913 (D_abs) chars at power 0.5 in swechat CC, 1778-2239 in aiv_cc; anything under 1k chars is free (TC16). It also must not touch an Edit/Write input that agent_changes copied. (b) Rewrite usage consistently. Recounting tokens with the provider tokenizer is cheap, and so is adding the delta to cache_read on every later response. But the frozen tally then stops matching at tolerance 0. Hiding that means rewriting the checkpoint commits on the entire/checkpoints branch, which is a force-push on any remote, and every fork that already copied the checkpoint (T9). The forger may not control those forks. The model never sees usage fields or the checkpoint branch. The forger can recompute everything except replicas they do not control. The tamper window before a freeze is the edit-to-commit lag: median 0.266 h [0.232, 0.302], p90 13.3 h (commit_witness O13). Push time is not in the data.
proposals.coverage: Measured: 4836 Claude-format sessions with api>0 have a tally, and 4794 match (T1). token_usage.api_call_count is filled in 12975/13406 checkpoint rows (raw_census A6-O6). Sessions linked to at least one ok commit: 4085/5850 = 0.698 [0.686, 0.710] (commit_witness O1). The share of tool results inside a frozen span is unmeasured. Prefix sessions leave a median of 3 messages unfrozen (T1). Only the SWE-chat/Entire repos have this; cc_local, aiv_cc and aiv_cu have no commit-time ledger.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. In effect this is hash-chain sealing (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric), supplied incidentally by git and an attribution tool installed for other reasons. Two parts might be new. First, the cache-chain amplification, where a usage-consistent 1-token edit shifts the frozen cache_read sum once per later response. Second, treating fork replicas as copies outside the forger's control. Probably close to prior art; check before claiming.
proposals.rank_reason: A tolerance-0 match against a snapshot held in replicated git turns rewriting usage from cheap arithmetic into a history rewrite. It only binds post-hoc tampering, and only in Entire-linked sessions.

proposals.name: Nested timer chain: durations printed in tool output must fit inside model-invisible harness timers, which must fit inside the provider interval of proposal 1
proposals.observation_summary: In honest swechat CC data, harness timers the model never sees are tight and violation-free. bash_progress elapsed obeys the floor rule in 0/112677 events (Wilson hi 3.41e-5, 687 sessions). Ticks advance by 1 s, the first tick lands at elapsed 3 (3211 calls) or 2 (2449), and the result follows the last tick in 5676/5676 (two_clocks O9). mcp_progress elapsed equals completed - started exactly in 1014/1147 and is never negative (two_clocks O2). Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch, Task and Agent timers sit inside the call->result window: Glob 1/2090, the others 0 (two_clocks O8). Timestamp latency agrees with harness duration at 0.985 [0.979, 0.989] (correlations O8). Codex writes a model-visible 'Wall time' header that never exceeds the call->output gap on exec_command (0 violations of 4408). It sits -139.24 to -49.65 ms from the exec duration, but that offset rests on 5 sessions, 1 of which supplies 1604/2420 rows. shell_command headers exceed the gap in 646/1817 cases by up to 49 ms, because they display 0.1 s rounding (two_clocks O6). Coverage limits: the progress stream exists in 1981/4925 swechat CC files and in 0 cc_local files (raw_census A6-O10), and harness durations exist for only 2.8% of CC calls (correlations O8). No lens measured durations printed inside tool output, such as test-runner summaries or `time`.
proposals.test_measurement: Data: swechat CC Bash results that have bash_progress (fix regexes and tolerance on split A, test on B), plus Codex exec outputs with both 'Wall time' and exec_command_end duration. Pre-register regexes for durations that tools print: pytest 'in X s', go test 'ok <pkg> Xs', cargo/jest/npm 'Finished in', 'Time:', 'Done in', and the shell `time` 'real' line. For each match, require D_print <= last-tick elapsed + 1 s and D_print <= the call->result gap, and require the gap <= S from proposal 1. Exclude re-read commands (cat/tail/head/grep of files) and background-task outputs. Report coverage (the share of shell results that print a duration), the honest violation rate with session-clustered CIs, and power against two simulated forgers. (i) A lying backend: keep the printed text, but give the call an instant-return timing profile drawn from honest calls that print no duration. (ii) A padded backend: sleep for D_print. This should pass, and it measures what the forger pays in wall-clock.
proposals.false_positive_source: Re-reads: in the commit-claim data, 15 of 19 out-of-window cases were cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files such as background-task .output files (commit_witness O11). Durations printed inside re-read logs belong to earlier runs, so command class must exclude them. Display rounding: 646/1817 Codex shell_command headers exceed the gap by up to 49 ms (two_clocks O6), so the tolerance must exceed the printed precision. Machine suspend: 1 progress event exceeded its timeout among 83521 (elapsed 901 s vs 300000 ms), and elapsed advanced with wall time in 377 of 378 long tick gaps (two_clocks O10). Long tails do not violate a ceiling: 435 of the 611 top-1% shell latencies run past their own timeout (D10). Unmeasured: runners that report cached results or cumulative times.
proposals.evasion_cost: Against a lying tool backend behind an honest harness: to print 'N passed in 45 s', the backend must actually take 45 s, because the harness measures bash_progress ticks and the call->result gap. The cost is real wall-clock per fake, or printing implausibly short durations. A forger who also controls the harness must regenerate a consistent 1 Hz tick chain: floored elapsed, a per-call phase lock (residual range median 6 ms), a first tick at 2-3 s, and timeoutMs equal to the argument. They must also regenerate durationMs and the timestamps. That is cheap to compute, and after that only proposal 1's provider interval still binds. The model sees its tool output, and in Codex the Wall time header. It does not see bash_progress, durationMs or mcp elapsed.
proposals.coverage: Harness side, measured: 112677 bash_progress events over 5702 calls in 687 sessions (two_clocks O9). The progress stream exists in 1981/4925 swechat CC files and 0/332 cc_local main files (raw_census A6-O10). Harness durations exist on 2.8% of CC calls (correlations O8), and Codex exec outputs carry a Wall time header in 4408 cases (two_clocks O6). The share of tool outputs that print a duration is unmeasured. Current Claude Code (cc_local) falls back to the call->result gap alone.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. METR-style recomputation checks what a command prints. My guess is that checking the time a tool claims it took against independent timers at two trust levels is less common. Part of this is ordinary log-consistency checking.
proposals.rank_reason: Model-invisible harness timers are tight enough to bound a lying tool server. But a forger who controls the harness defeats them, current Claude Code no longer writes them, and the content side is unmeasured.

proposals.name: Prompt-cache state as a server-computed stopwatch and unchanged-prefix certificate
proposals.observation_summary: The provider reports how much of each request matched its prompt cache. The chain cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds in 59747/59804 aiv_cc clean pairs. Breaks track elapsed time: 49/59772 pairs break at gaps under 300 s, against 8/32 at 300 s or more. Image pairs hold in 4367/4570, compaction pairs in 0/933 (aiv_accounting O9). The exact chain holds in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1). Unlogged history edits surface as resets. In 30 non-compaction pairs across 12 aiv_cc runs, cache_read resets to 20401-21400 (the system prefix) with no compact_boundary row; 0/30 carry a context_management object, and 27/30 are image pairs (aiv_accounting O12). In swechat CC, the 616 clean pairs with a cache_read drop exceed the conservation threshold at 0.166 vs 0.009, and they are 47 of the 71 pairs with |r| > 20000 (TC12). Model switches force misses: 69/89 overall and 40/43 on a switch to Haiku, but only 15/31 on a return from Haiku (changepoints O9). A missing harness channel produces unexplained drops: aiv_cu SDK drops sit 5.9-13.4 s from compaction rows that only aiv_cc logs (changepoints O8). aiv_cc has no decodable server id (ids O13), so cache state is its only server-side time signal.
proposals.test_measurement: (a) TTL curve: in swechat CC, estimate P(cache-chain break) as a function of the skew-free server interval S from proposal 1, per model; in aiv_cc, as a function of the created_at gap. Pre-register the gap bins on split A. (b) Retiming test on split B: shift a random round's client timestamps by +/-k minutes while keeping usage, and report how often the (gap bin, break/hit) pair becomes implausible under the split-A curve. (c) Unchanged-prefix certificate: flag pairs where cache_read(k+1) < cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) and no logged compaction, image, model switch or above-TTL gap is present. Report per-corpus counts against the honest aiv_cc count of 30 (aiv_accounting O12), and join across tables before flagging (changepoints O8).
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: idle gaps of 300 s or more break only 8/32 pairs, so a cache hit after a long claimed gap is not evidence (aiv_accounting O9). Image pairs hold only 4367/4570, and compaction pairs 0/933 (aiv_accounting O9). Client-side pruning leaves no log marker (30 resets, aiv_accounting O12). Model switches miss 69/89, and returns to a recent model often hit (only 15/31 miss) (changepoints O9). Some compactions are logged only in another table (changepoints O8). Unmeasured: cache TTL tiers and refresh-on-hit rules, and proxies that do not pass cache fields through.
proposals.evasion_cost: A post-hoc forger who retimes a round but leaves usage alone creates either a break at a short gap or a hit pattern at odds with the claimed gap. Only the first is informative (base rate 49/59772). Compressing a real long gap is therefore caught only when the provider actually expired the cache, which happened in 8/32 long gaps in aiv_cc. A forger who rewrites usage needs only arithmetic and a guess at the TTL rules. A guess of 'hit' is safe because long-gap hits are common. A live forger who silently rewrites earlier history before sending a request (for example, to hide a failed tool result from the model) gets a provider-computed cache_read that resets to the edit point. They must also rewrite the logged usage. That is cheap unless usage is frozen (proposal 2) or reconciled against provider billing, which is not in the data. The model never sees cache fields.
proposals.coverage: Every consecutive response pair with usage: 59804 clean aiv_cc pairs in 190 runs of one agent (aiv_accounting O9). TC1's pipeline has 154189 swechat CC pairs, 30210 cc_local pairs and 35307 aiv_cc pairs. Providers that report no cache fields are not covered.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Prompt-cache hits are known as a timing side channel in security work. I have not seen anyone read the provider's reported cache_read as a certificate of how much history was unchanged, or as a coarse server-side stopwatch for logs that carry no server ids. Low confidence.
proposals.rank_reason: Server-computed, invisible to the model, and the only server-side timing in aiv_cc. But long gaps seldom force a miss (8/32), and the cache arithmetic is cheap for a forger to recompute.

proposals.name: Provider quantization lattices in usage fields as a trap for synthesized rounds
proposals.observation_summary: Provider-computed usage numbers sit on undocumented lattices. Codex cached_input_tokens is a multiple of 128 in 16106/16106 calls. So are OpenCode per-message cache reads for GPT/OpenAI-family models (11393/11393), but only 1/563 for Claude models (T11). Gemini IMAGE prompt tokens move by 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11668/11668 pairs. They increase in 5059/5092 GUI windows and in 0 shell (0/4134) or get_pixel_coords (0/2033) windows (TC9). The unit is set by model generation: 258 for gemini-2.5-pro, 1064 for 3.x, and a third constant, 2160, in 3 sessions; no session mixes lattices (0/309) (D3). Uncached input collapses onto a per-model constant: opus-4-6 takes value 1 in 0.835 of responses, and aiv_cc shows 8 x30427 and 10 x5024 (D7). Codex reasoning tokens pile onto 516 + 518k, with no known mechanism; 140/6910 rows are on the lattice (D1).
proposals.test_measurement: From split A, fix lattice rules per (provider, model generation): Codex/OpenAI cached tokens % 128 == 0; Gemini dIMAGE in {0, unit(model)} with unit in {258, 1064, 2160}; Gemini dIMAGE > 0 iff the window contains a screenshot-returning action; the CC usage_in mode by model. On split B, report the honest violation rate per rule. Forgery simulation: insert synthetic rounds whose usage comes from (i) a chars/4 forger and (ii) a forger who copies neighbouring usage and adds a tokenizer delta but ignores the lattices. Report the detection rate per insertion.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: OpenCode routes through several providers, so its session totals sit on the 128 lattice only 569/619 (T11). Claude usage shows no 128 granularity (49/4785 sessions, T11). 33 of 5092 Gemini GUI windows show no image increment, unexplained. The no-pruning rule is untested beyond 40 images, and gemini-3.8-flash never has an image (TC9). haiku-4-5 has no dominant usage_in value (D7). Lattice constants change with model generation.
proposals.evasion_cost: Very cheap once known: round cached tokens to 128, add one model-specific image unit per fabricated screenshot, and copy the model's usage_in constant. The forger has to learn each constant from honest logs of the same model. The 2160 unit appeared in only 3 sessions, and the 516 + 518k lattice has no known cause. A live forger who sends a fake screenshot gets a real increment from the provider. The model does not see usage fields. This trap catches only forgers who synthesize usage for inserted rounds without studying honest logs.
proposals.coverage: Codex calls with usage: 16106 (T11). OpenCode GPT-family messages: 11393 (T11). aiv_cu Gemini pairs: 11945 (TC9). Anthropic cache fields are not covered.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Plausibility checks on value distributions (Benford-style) are old. Using provider-specific usage lattices to catch synthesized model turns is probably unpublished, but the check is weak enough that novelty matters little.
proposals.rank_reason: Exact in honest data and invisible to the model. But each lattice is a constant a forger can copy, so it stops only forgers who have not studied honest logs.
